claims.text: Increasing substrate surface energy enhances adhesion of PtPdCuNiAu precursors.
Increasing substrate surface energy reduces precursor or atomic diffusion during nucleation.
Inhibiting precursor mobility during low-temperature HEA nanoparticle formation favors formation of a single phase.
Reduced mobility kinetically traps the PtPdCuNiAu nanoparticles in a homogeneous single-phase alloy state.
A high-surface-energy oxide substrate acts as a diffusion barrier at the nanoparticle–substrate interface.
Limiting atomic rearrangement suppresses stress-induced diffusion and phase segregation during nucleation.
Kinetic trapping caused by low mobility promotes uniform intermixing of the constituent metals.
Formation of a homogeneous HEA phase produces highly dispersed or isolated catalytic active sites.
High dispersion of Pt and Pd active sites contributes to enhanced catalytic activity.
PtPdCuNiAu nanoparticles synthesized on a higher-surface-energy substrate will be more homogeneous and more consistently single-phase than those synthesized on a lower-surface-energy substrate.
PtPdCuNiAu nanoparticles synthesized on a higher-surface-energy substrate will have better-dispersed active sites.
PtPdCuNiAu nanoparticles synthesized on a higher-surface-energy substrate will exhibit higher catalytic yield than particles synthesized on a lower-surface-energy substrate.
PtPdCuNiAu nanoparticles synthesized on a higher-surface-energy substrate will exhibit lower catalytic activation energy than the baseline particles.
Lower-surface-energy substrates permit greater precursor mobility and consequently increase the propensity for localized phase separation.
Pre-treated SiO2 provides a higher-surface-energy substrate than untreated or modified Al2O3 in the proposed comparison.
Substrate-induced modulation of precursor mobility is expected to be a dominant formation factor for low-temperature colloidal synthesis of PtPdCuNiAu nanoparticles on oxide substrates.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis says substrate surface energy is the sole variable, but the proposed comparison changes the substrate from SiO2 to Al2O3. This also changes substrate composition and interfacial chemistry, so the design does not isolate surface energy.
